title: Ultraslow Relaxation of Toroidal State in Ferrotoroidal Dysprosium Complex

material_class.structural_family: tridecanuclear hourglass {GaDy} core between two {Ga3} triangles; two {Dy3} triangles with a ferrotoroidal ground state

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, Ga(NO3)3·xH2O (0.255 g, 1 mmol) and Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.212 g, 0.5 mmol) in acetonitrile (20 mL) were treated with N-methyldiethanolamine (0.120 mL, 1 mmol), chloroacetic acid (0.250 g, 0.5 mmol), and triethylamine (0.6 mL, 5 mmol). The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 24 h to a white solution, the solvent was removed under reduced pressure to a colorless gel, and the gel was redissolved in 1:1 MeOH/iPrOH and evaporated slowly at ambient temperature. Colorless crystals formed after 15–20 days (main text: 3–4 weeks). The crystals are air-stable; a slight excess of chloroacetic acid gives a different complex.
synthesis.time: 24 h stirring; crystals after 15–20 days (main text 3–4 weeks)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic stirring, solvent removal under reduced pressure, then slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: colorless gel redissolved in 1:1 MeOH/iPrOH and slowly evaporated to colorless single crystals

properties.summary: Discrete heterometallic ferrotoroidal single-molecule toroic. DC data show antiferromagnetic/anisotropic behavior and an S-shaped low-field magnetization curve. AC susceptibility shows no zero-field out-of-phase signal but field-induced two-step Orbach relaxation under 2400 Oe. μSQUID hysteresis and angle-dependent maps confirm a nonmagnetic FT ground state; a slow component has a QTM time of about 3.5×10^8 s (~11 years), among the longest reported for a molecular magnet.
